name: Deterministic Workflow
summary: Keep ordering, routing, retry, termination and output ownership in code while bounding semantic model work inside typed nodes.
context: Mandatory ordering, fan-out, retry, approval or loop invariants must survive model variation.
Execution path, failure and resume behavior must be observable.
forces: Explicit control adds nodes and schemas but makes policy independently testable.
Replay requires stable node identity and idempotent external effects.
An external workflow engine may still own long-lived distributed durability.
decision: Represent business control as graph edges and typed nodes.
Give every retry and terminal outcome one explicit owner.
Keep semantic model work bounded inside nodes rather than using it as the control plane.
implementation: Use FunctionNode and typed join payloads for deterministic work.
Route success, rejection and loop exhaustion explicitly.
Persist Event evidence and make external side effects idempotent.
Delegate one logical output owner to avoid duplicate terminal Events.

observable_contract.statement: Ordering, routing and terminal outcomes are visible in graph structure and Event node paths.
A downstream node runs only after required branch outputs are joined into a typed payload.
One narrow node owns retry and emits observable failure evidence before recovery or exhaustion.
Resume may re-surface output without repeating an external effect, and output ownership remains singular.

failure_modes.statement: A technical loop bound is treated as business success or rejection instead of an explicit route.
Framework, node and tool retries stack without one budget or idempotency owner.
Missing join state or duplicate parent and child outputs remain hidden until a downstream consumer fails.
Renamed nodes or non-idempotent side effects make historical Session replay unsafe.

counterexamples.context: One deterministic operation has no branching, retry or persisted resume requirement.
counterexamples.preferred: Use a normal function or service call.

counterexamples.context: The work is a single bounded semantic transformation.
counterexamples.preferred: Use one single-turn Agent node with typed input and output.

adk_versions.notes: Graph Workflow, FunctionNode, JoinNode, RetryConfig and replay were exercised at the pinned commit.
SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent and LoopAgent remain comparison evidence but have different parent-continuation semantics.

source_evidence.claim: Workflow schedules triggers, joins, routed loops, checkpoints and replay.
NodeRunner owns node-local timeout, retry, error Event and output flushing.
ReplayManager reconstructs completed child executions from persisted Events.
Legacy max_iterations is a technical execution bound rather than a domain outcome.

lab_evidence.claim: Tests cover sequence, fan-out, join, loop routes, missing state and output delegation.
Tests distinguish node retry, legacy child failure and explicit loop exhaustion.
Fresh graph objects resume without repeating the external ledger effect.

rejected_decisions.decision: Use an LLM coordinator to choose a route already defined by business policy.
rejected_decisions.reason: Model variation makes mandatory ordering and terminal behavior non-deterministic.
rejected_decisions.replacement: Encode fixed control in Workflow edges and reserve model calls for bounded semantic nodes.
